concerns.text: The idea expects a dataset of >500 individuals across >10 species to achieve adequate power, but the specification only measures the proportion of merged records (SC-001) and does not require meeting the absolute sample‑size threshold.

The idea’s expected results mention assessing heterogeneity of effect sizes in a meta‑analytic framework, yet the spec provides only a single pooled LMM with no meta‑analysis or heterogeneity assessment.

The functional requirement FR‑001 mandates inclusion of `body_mass_g` in the merged dataset, but body mass is never used in any model or analysis. The original idea does not request body mass as a covariate, so this adds an unrequested feature.

The spec adds a memory‑limit edge case (switching to chunked processing when RAM > 6 GB). The idea makes no mention of such compute constraints; this engineering safeguard is outside the defined research scope.

The handling of records with `migration_status = "Unknown"` (retaining them in the base model but excluding from interaction terms) is not described in the idea. This exclusion rule changes the analysis plan beyond what was requested.

Success Criterion SC-002 uses the model’s own p‑value (< 0.05) to flag significance, i.e., it validates the model by the same statistic the model produces. This is a circular validation because the predictor (telomere‑length coefficient) and the validation target (p‑value) are not independent; the p‑value is a deterministic function of the fitted model.

responses.response: Added explicit sample‑size requirement (≥500 individuals across ≥10 species) to SC‑001 and introduced FR‑011 to enforce this check.
